items.text: The BLS reported that the US added 165,000 nonfarm jobs in October, well above forecasts (Reuters said more than twice what economists expected) and far above the 48,000 monthly average of the previous year. Unemployment was 4.1% (7.1 million people). August was revised up to +186,000 and September to +60,000, a combined 84,000 more than first reported. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% on the year, to $38.00. Gains came mainly in professional and business services (+70,000), health care (+42,000), transportation and warehousing (+25,000) and manufacturing (+19,000). Participation held at 61.9%, and 2.0 million people (27.6% of the unemployed) had been out of work for 27 weeks or more.
items.notes: The figures are the official BLS release. CNBC also flagged that long-term unemployment is rising, though we could not open that article.

items.text: After the jobs report, markets put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rate hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting at about 85%, up from about 75% before, Reuters reported. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly told CNBC she expects the Fed will have to tighten further to bring down inflation she called too high. She described the tech-stock repricing as painful but orderly. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said policymakers would watch how the data accumulates. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.86%.
items.notes: Note the direction: the Fed is in a tightening cycle, and the debate is about raising rates, not cutting them. Our sources did not give the current target range.

items.text: Chip stocks partly recovered on Nov 6 after Thursday's rout: Nvidia rose about 6% and AMD about 8%. The Nasdaq closed up 1.09% at 24,579 and the S&P 500 up 0.31% at 7,377, while the Dow fell 0.46% to 51,286. The S&P 500 still had its worst week since June, with tech down about 7% and energy about 11% on the week. Brent settled around $98 and WTI around $91. Tesla said it will wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027.
items.reporter: Grace O'Donnell, David Hollerith, Ines Ferré
items.notes: Estimates of the value wiped out on Nov 5 vary: Yahoo says about $3tn, earlier reports $2.3–2.5tn. The oil settlement prices come from Gulf News.

items.text: AP, citing two Middle East officials, reported that Iran is reviewing a Qatari 'bridge' proposal of two days of trust-building steps. On day one the US would lift its port blockade and release some frozen funds, and Iran would admit IAEA inspectors to bombed sites. On day two Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz under a modified Iran–Oman arrangement that Washington has not approved, before wider talks on Iran's roughly 441 kg of 60%-enriched uranium. A senior Iranian official and security official Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran will neither reopen Hormuz nor negotiate until seven conditions are met, including lifting sanctions, unfreezing assets and paying war reparations. Trump said the US is 'talking to Iran', and the White House declined to comment on the proposal.
items.notes: The details come from unnamed officials. Earlier reports described a three-day sequence, while AP describes two days. Fox News (relayed by The National) said CENTCOM was finalising preparations for a possible operation, but no order had been given.

items.text: Trump said in the Oval Office that he would decide soon between resuming operations against Iran and a deal, adding that he would rather not destroy the rest of the country but might have to. Fox News reported that Central Command was finalising preparations for a possible operation, but no order had been issued. Iran's Rezaei met Vladimir Putin in Moscow with a message from the supreme leader, and Putin reportedly offered to help end the conflict.
items.notes: The Trump–emir call and the 'destroy the rest' remark were already logged on Nov 5-6. What is new here is the CENTCOM report (Fox, relayed) and the Rezaei–Putin meeting.

items.text: Gulf News reports that one crew member died on the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker MT Velos Sapphire. The tanker was hit by an explosion on Nov 5 while sailing empty toward Bahrain. The operator suspects a missile but has not confirmed the cause. The fire is out and no pollution was reported.
items.notes: This is probably the same Nov 5 incident UKMTO reported (two projectiles, about 50 nm north of Qatar); the death is new. Gulf News also mentions a Trump statement about limited strikes near Qeshm. That may be the Nov 3 strike already logged, so it is not logged as new.

items.text: Democrat Scott Colom's lead over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith grew to 2,010 votes (466,959 to 465,023) in AP results at 12:30pm ET on Nov 6, up from about 1,140 on Nov 5. Secretary of State Michael Watson estimated 12,000–20,000 affidavit ballots are still uncounted, more than usual because of voter-roll maintenance, and said about 76% are being accepted. Colom criticised Watson's office for using Experian commercial data to check voter rolls. Mississippi Today and Axios report that roughly 230,000 registrations were inactivated and are now under scrutiny. No lawsuit had been filed, though the state GOP chair said Republicans would act swiftly if they found violations.
items.notes: Democracy Docket leans left, but the vote figures are AP's. The 230,000 figure comes from an Axios headline we could not open. Watson says county commissioners, not his office, change voter status.

items.text: Alaska's Senate count has not been updated since Wednesday: Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan 102,962 to 102,325 (637 votes), with about a quarter of ballots outstanding. Peltola's campaign says the remaining early and absentee ballots will widen her lead. A Sullivan campaign memo argues he would win ranked-choice tabulation on current votes and calls the race the biggest election cheating scandal in Alaska's history, citing a New York Times report that the Peltola campaign denies. Ranked-choice tabulation starts Nov 18.
items.notes: We did not see the NYT report the Sullivan memo cites. Reason (libertarian) argues Peltola appears likely to win.

items.text: Democrats have reached 253 House seats to Republicans' 157, with 25 races still uncalled as of Friday morning, according to an Anadolu tally of US media projections. The AP called New York's 17th District early on Nov 6. The tally implies a large Democratic majority in the next House, which convenes Jan 3.
items.notes: Anadolu does not name the outlet whose projections it counts. Check the numbers against AP or CBS before using them in headlines.

items.text: Opposition to Chuck Schumer as Democratic leader is widening among newcomers. Democracy Now lists senators-elect Peggy Flanagan, Troy Jackson, Abdul El-Sayed, Juliana Stratton and Adam Hamilton, plus Mississippi candidate Scott Colom, as saying they will not back him. Texas senator-elect James Talarico refuses to commit and wants the filibuster abolished. Schumer told CNN 'the issue is not me' and that he will be re-elected leader, and a Washington Post analysis says he is poised to keep the post.
items.notes: Democracy Now is left-leaning. We saw only the Washington Post headline (paywalled). The leadership vote is expected in December.

items.text: Ahead of the lame-duck session on Nov 9, House Democrats are planning votes in their first 100 hours next year. HNGN reports they would restore enhanced ACA subsidies, reverse about $1tn in Medicaid cuts by their estimate, undo Trump's tariffs and end or limit the Iran war. In the lame duck itself, the administration seeks a record $1.5tn for defence, which Senate Democrats reject, and Republicans are weighing a debt-limit increase before Jan 3.
items.notes: HNGN is a small aggregator. The Hill (which we could not open) reports that Trump's lame-duck agenda is stalling.

items.text: After this week's AI-stock sell-off, some institutional investors have reportedly told bankers that a $1.5–1.6tn valuation for Anthropic's IPO would be appropriate, down from the roughly $2tn discussed earlier. Business Standard and TheStreet reported this, as relayed by Tech Insider. Reuters reports that the planned November listing and next week's roadshow are under investor scrutiny. No delay has been announced, and no price range had been filed as of the latest reports. Anthropic's last private valuation was $965bn in May.
items.notes: The valuation feedback is second-hand, from unnamed sources. City AM's headline said the IPO is 'in doubt', but no delay is confirmed. This desk is produced with Anthropic's Claude.

items.text: AAA's national average for regular gasoline was about $4.10 a gallon and diesel about $6.26, down slightly. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan said that, after this week's slump in fuel futures and what he called very high political pressure after the midterms, gasoline could fall to about $3.65 and diesel to about $5.50 in the coming weeks. Separately, DOE awarded contracts on Nov 4 to exchange 300,000 barrels from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve under emergency authority, citing supply-chain disruptions.
items.notes: The GasBuddy figure is a forecast, not a guarantee. The DOE exchange must be repaid with a premium before the 2027-28 winter.

items.text: FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford will testify before the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee next week (Nov 10) on the $12.5bn air-traffic-control overhaul Congress approved in 2025. The administration wants $30bn more, which major airlines back, but it is unclear whether the outgoing Congress will provide it. A recent government report said more money is needed to finish phase one. The FAA aims to replace floppy disks at more than 400 facilities and phase out paper flight strips by 2028.
items.notes: The testimony date is inferred from 'Tuesday' and 'next week'.

items.text: In an unsigned order with no noted dissents, the Supreme Court denied the Trump administration's emergency request in United States v. California (26A624). The administration wanted California to set aside ballots from suspected noncitizen voters until their citizenship was verified. Lower courts (Judge David Carter on Oct 28 and the Ninth Circuit on Oct 30) had already refused, with Carter questioning the government's allegations.
items.notes: The order is from Nov 2, before this window, but it was not logged earlier. It is relevant to the GOP's push to segregate affidavit ballots in Mississippi.

items.text: Trump signed a proclamation, the 'American Declaration of Freedom in Space', declaring outer space open to exploration, development and permanent settlement by US citizens, consistent with US law and international obligations. It restates goals of returning to the Moon by 2028, establishing a permanent lunar presence and landing Americans on Mars. It says Artemis III is planned for next summer, and it assigns no new tasks to agencies.
items.notes: Signed Nov 3 and found on whitehouse.gov in this run; not logged earlier. It is largely symbolic.

items.text: No major new FDA food recalls appeared in this window. Recall roundups for Nov 6 show the CPSC recalling Gourmia GTF7530 air fryer ovens sold at Target, because the doors can swing shut and cause burns, and Magnetopia magnetic building cubes over a magnet-swallowing hazard. The CPSC also warned about Fire Blaze lighters and HAIARA W5 PRO power banks sold online.
items.notes: The Brad's kale chips (thallium) and Macleods blood-pressure drug recalls were already logged.

items.text: On the evening of Nov 6, S&P Global affirmed Poland's foreign-currency rating at A-/A-2 but changed the outlook from stable to negative. It also cut the local-currency rating from A/A-1 to A-/A-2. According to the Finance Ministry's communiqué relaying S&P, the agency expects the general government deficit to stay above 7% of GDP until 2027 because elections will slow consolidation, and net debt to exceed 70% of GDP by 2029, up from 53% in 2025. S&P also cites President Nawrocki's veto power as an obstacle to the government's fiscal plans; Moody's had already cut Poland to A3 in September.
items.thread: Poland public finances and credit ratings
items.notes: The decision came after US market close on Friday, so the market reaction will only show on Monday Nov 9. WNP puts the 10-year yield at about 6.12% on Friday. VeloBank's Piotr Arak expects yields to stay high rather than jump. The base case (an affirmation with a stable outlook) did not happen.

items.text: Finance Minister Andrzej Domański blamed President Nawrocki for the S&P outlook cut. Polsat News reports he pointed to S&P's own statement that presidential vetoes limit the Tusk government's legislative and fiscal plans. He said the government would keep strengthening public finances despite the vetoes. The ministry added that policymaking is harder in the run-up to elections.
items.notes: wPolityce's headline (the page could not be fetched) calls the decision a 'powerful blow to the Tusk government' and mocks Domański for 'finding a culprit'. Liberal and centrist outlets lead on S&P's own reference to vetoes. No reaction from the Presidential Palace was found by early Nov 7.

items.text: On Nov 6 the Sejm rejected PiS's no-confidence motion against Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński, with 212 votes for, 235 against and none abstaining (231 were needed to remove him). PiS, Konfederacja, Rozwój Plus, Razem and several small circles backed the motion, while KO, PSL, Lewica, Centrum and Polska 2050 voted against it as a bloc. The motion accused him of politicising the police, including deploying officers at the Constitutional Tribunal, and of failures on the public warning system and cybercrime staffing. Tusk said Kierwiński stays because he pursues criminals and guards the borders.
items.notes: Right-leaning niezalezna.pl foregrounds PiS's Czarnek, who said more than 1,000 police were brought to the Tribunal without knowing their task, and gives Tusk's defence only briefly. PAP and centrist outlets give both sides. Razem voting with the right is notable. TVN24 and Wyborcza coverage could not be retrieved.

items.text: Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, acting as head of the Constitutional Tribunal, called a General Assembly of its judges for Nov 17. The assembly will consider the Prosecutor General's motions to lift the immunity of suspended Tribunal President Bogdan Święczkowski (six motions) and Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański (one). According to PAP, as reported by Rzeczpospolita, the motions against Święczkowski concern Pegasus and Hermes spyware, blocking Sejm-elected judges from adjudicating, and unlawful delegation of prosecutors while he was National Prosecutor. One motion also seeks consent to detain him and to apply for his pre-trial arrest.
items.notes: The Presidential Palace and the Święczkowski camp do not recognise Korwin-Piotrowska's authority to convene assemblies, and the Palace earlier said it would notify prosecutors over her previous assembly. No reaction to the Nov 17 date was found by early Nov 7. A separate assembly she called for Nov 10 is still pending (W-261105-05).

items.text: Korwin-Piotrowska said that in 2026 Święczkowski did not hear, act as rapporteur on, or rule on any citizens' constitutional complaint. By her account, he issued only rulings on presidential motions, four of them as rapporteur. She cited a complaint filed in January 2017 that has sat untouched since 2019, and promised that pending cases would now proceed in turn. No response from Święczkowski was reported.
items.notes: These are one side's claims and have not been independently verified.

items.text: The full Senate passed the anti-alcohol bill with amendments, so it returns to the Sejm. The bill bans retail alcohol sales from 22:00 to 06:00 nationwide and bans most alcohol advertising, and the Senate moved its start to June 2027. An amendment allowing advertising of non-alcoholic beer passed by a single vote, 46–45. Other amendments allow night sales at airports and some advertising in wholesalers, restaurants and specialist shops. A proposed ban on home delivery of online alcohol orders was rejected, while the ban on discounts, bundles and loyalty schemes stays.
items.notes: Rzeczpospolita says the Senate passed it unanimously. Unlike the committee proposal reported earlier, the home-delivery ban was not adopted. The Health Ministry had opposed the 0% beer change.

items.text: President Karol Nawrocki announced on X that he will join the Nov 11 Independence March in Warsaw, as he does every year. The march's slogan is 'Polak w Polsce gospodarzem' ('A Pole is the host in Poland'). Organisers expect 500,000 or more, and say bus bookings are three times last year's. Rzeczpospolita reports that the Constitutional Tribunal dispute and anti-EU slogans will feature.
items.notes: The attendance figure is the organisers' estimate. Police and city hall counts are usually lower, and Rzeczpospolita puts the usual turnout at about 200,000.

items.text: The Energy Minister's notice (Monitor Polski item 1101) caps fuel prices for Saturday Nov 7 through Monday Nov 9. The caps are 6.12 zł/l for 95 petrol (down 8 gr), 6.80 zł for 98 (down 13 gr) and 7.83 zł for diesel (down 8 gr). The 'Ceny Paliwa Niżej' programme is still due to end on Dec 31, and no extension has been announced.
items.notes: The primary notice is MP 2026 item 1101, but the official text was not opened.

items.text: CBOS's November poll (fieldwork Nov 2–4, 1,000 respondents) puts KO at 28.1%, PiS at 15.8% (down 2.4 points) and Konfederacja at 15.4% (up 2.6). Braun's Konfederacja Korony Polskiej has 7.8% and Nowa Lewica 5.9%. Coalition partners PSL (1.8%) and Polska 2050 (1.1%) are far below the 5% threshold, and 14.2% are undecided.
items.notes: Fieldwork came just after the Oct 30 Tribunal takeover. The margin of error was not reported.

items.text: Chinese fashion platform Shein will invest €500m (2.2bn zł) to expand its logistics hub in Magnice near Wrocław, which has run since 2022. Notes from Poland, citing Wroclaw.pl, reports about 2,000 new jobs by the end of 2026, bringing the site to roughly 10,000, along with 6,500 sorting robots. Shein says the expansion will cut European delivery times to as little as 48 hours. It comes as the EU tightens fees on low-value parcels from China.
items.notes: This was announced Nov 5 but missed in the previous run. The jobs figure comes from a local city news service, and no response from Polish officials was reported.

items.text: According to a PAP headline from the evening of Nov 6, Poland will fund the purchase of electricity generators for Ukraine. The amount and channel were not available because the article could not be opened. The announcement came the same day Ukrainian FM Sybiha visited Warsaw for the Council of the Baltic Sea States meeting.
items.notes: Only the headline was seen; the details need checking.

items.text: Wisła Kraków beat Cracovia 2-1 in the 204th Kraków derby at the Reymonta stadium. Marc Carbo scored in the 9th minute, Ajdin Hasic equalised from a penalty rebound in the 20th, and Marko Bozic scored the winner in first-half stoppage time. Pyrotechnics from the stands caused stoppages and 12 minutes of added time in the first half. Cracovia's Mateusz Klich was sent off in the 93rd minute for kicking Jeremy Guillemenot. Wisła moved up to fifth, while Cracovia, on 12 points from 14 games, is near the relegation zone.
items.notes: Wisła captain Alan Uryga called Klich's foul scandalous; Klich admitted it was a stupid foul (LoveKraków). The length of Klich's ban is not yet known. No official police tally for derby night was found for this match; a policja.pl item reporting 21 detentions after a derby is undated and may refer to an earlier game, so it was not used.

items.text: Mayor Łukasz Gibała confirmed on Friday evening that the city will stop publishing its monthly paper Kraków.pl at the end of 2026, after about 18 years. He said it cost the city 2.5m zł in 2026: about 1.6m zł for printing, about 648,000 zł for mailbox delivery and about 103,000 zł for kiosk sales. Under his predecessor Aleksander Miszalski the print run had risen from about 30,000 to 220,000 copies. LoveKraków first reported the plan unofficially on Nov 2.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Gazeta Krakowska says the short announcement leaves more questions than answers, for example about city TV and any replacement bulletin. Councillor Dydyńska-Czesak (Kraków dla Mieszkańców) wants a short information bulletin instead.

items.text: Former mayor Aleksander Miszalski criticised Gibała's first two weeks. He put the announced savings at about 17m zł a year: dropped memberships about 8m, Mayor's Office budget 3.6m, Kraków.pl 2.5m, abolished departments 2m and envoys up to 0.75m. He said that is outweighed by at least 30m zł a year in lost revenue from restoring the 20-minute ticket and the 90 zł monthly pass. He also questioned appointments made without competitions, including the new supervisory board of Krakowski Holding Komunalny.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: These are Miszalski's own estimates; the article includes no reply from Gibała.

items.text: Gibała issued an order creating a new post: mayor's envoy for legal violations, based in the Mayor's Chancellery and reporting to him directly. The envoy is to report suspected crimes, monitor public-finance discipline, work with the tax department on suspected money laundering, coordinate whistleblower procedures and run anti-corruption training. No appointee has been named. Earlier, Gibała dismissed five previous envoys.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor

items.text: Former Kraków mayor Prof. Andrzej Gołaś reportedly resigned as chair of the supervisory board of the city company Arena Kraków and left the board. According to one board member, he wanted to dismiss long-serving CEO Małgorzata Marcińska, a PSL member, but the board did not back him. Arena was flagged in this week's NIK audit for about 606,000 zł in board pay above the statutory cap.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Unofficial, from a single board member; neither the company nor the city confirmed it.

items.text: A day after the regional environment directorate (RDOŚ) found violations, Deputy Mayor Karol Wałachowski, the city's animal-welfare spokesperson and municipal guards inspected the Ruczaj site near ul. Obozowa. They confirmed heavy-machinery earthworks inside the beaver habitat, which the city says departed from the approved plans. The city filed its own police notification and ordered permanent municipal-guard patrols. It also asked University of Agriculture scientists to count the beavers. The developer had earlier asked to cull six beavers and remove their dams, then withdrew the request.
items.notes: ATAL said beforehand that it had not received the RDOŚ letter and was not working in the beaver pond area; there was no post-inspection response. The city defends the building permit as consistent with the 2021 'Kobierzyńska' local plan, which identified no protected species.

items.text: GDDKiA picked a consortium of Kraków firms ZUE, Energopol and Sarivo, which bid 76.6m zł, to build a two-level interchange replacing the dangerous junction on the Zakopianka (DK7) at Jawornik near Myślenice. Ten firms bid, and the highest offer was about 101.75m zł. The contract will be signed once the choice is final, as rivals can still appeal. Work is expected to take about 28 months including winter breaks, with drivers using the interchange from spring 2029.
items.notes: The contract is not yet signed, and rival bidders can still appeal.

items.text: From Nov 7 to 15, the right-hand lane of ul. Nowohucka towards Nowa Huta is closed before the junction with ul. Koszykarska. The contractor is building a storm sewer and must first expose power, fibre and signal cables by hand. The developer-funded rebuild of Nowohucka, which adds a U-turn lane towards Stoczniowców and Saska, is due to finish around late March or early April 2027.

ZTP announced that from Monday, Nov 9, every second run of replacement bus line 704 to Bronowice Małe will run as the new line 714. Line 714 takes a slightly longer route via Nowy Kleparz, Politechnika, Dworzec Główny Zachód and Teatr Słowackiego, giving a direct link to the main station. Lines 704 and 708 otherwise stay the same. Also from Nov 9, the Prądnik Czerwony P+R 01 stop closes for repairs, affecting lines 105, 128, 184, 193, 199, 250, 405, 442 and 610.

The KL Plaszow Memorial Museum signed a contract of about 2.5m zł with the Kraków firm New Amsterdam for its permanent exhibition. The firm had been the cheapest bidder but was initially rejected, and it won after appeals to the National Appeals Chamber (KIO). The exhibition is due to open in mid-2027. The whole memorial project costs over 61m zł, nearly 45m zł of it from EU funds.

Two city sports facilities opened. One is the covered Lodowa Arena KSOS ice rink on ul. Kordylewskiego, which cost 25.5m zł; skating costs 16 zł (12 zł reduced) per hour-long session. The other is a full-size artificial-turf pitch with a club building for MKS Wolica on ul. Plażowa, which cost about 8.7m zł, 3m zł of it from the government's Sportowa Polska programme.
items.notes: The ice rink article (published Nov 3) announced the Nov 6 opening; the opening itself was not separately confirmed.

items.text: IMGW issued first-degree (yellow) fog warnings for most of Małopolska, excluding Tatra county, from 18:00 Friday to 10:00 Saturday, with visibility below 200 m and freezing fog possible on roads. More fog is expected on Sunday morning, and the night into Sunday could bring frost of about -2 to -4°C. Daytime highs over the weekend are about 4-9°C. With calm, cold weather, aqicn data showed PM2.5 in Kraków reaching an 'unhealthy' level (US AQI 158) early on Nov 6.
items.notes: Air-quality reading is from aqicn (US EPA scale), not GIOŚ, which could not be checked directly; no official smog alert for Kraków was found.

items.text: On Nov 6 the Election Commission told the chief electoral officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland to give voters marked 'absent, shifted, dead or duplicate' (ASDD) in the SIR another chance to get onto the final rolls. Booth-wise ASDD lists, with the likely reason for exclusion, are to be put up again at polling stations and panchayat and municipal offices and posted on CEO websites. Booth officers are to do house-to-house visits with party agents. Voters who moved within the state can file with their new address and no Form 8, and homeless voters can rely on a booth officer's field report as proof of residence. Congress's Jairam Ramesh called it another 'U-turn' and an admission that voters were wrongly struck off, repeating the party's claim that over 13 crore people lost their vote.
items.outlet: PTI (via Kashmir Reader); Business Standard Hindi
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: PTI, ANI and Business Standard Hindi agree on the order's content. No deadline was reported. The ECI frames the order as making sure no eligible voter is left out, while Congress reads it as admitting error. The 13-crore figure is Congress's claim, not ECI data. ECI's own release was not found.

items.text: ThePrint Hindi reports that 2,06,88,487 names were removed from Maharashtra's draft rolls, published Aug 31 for all 288 assembly seats. By Nov 1, 14.1 lakh Form-6 applications had come in, including from first-time voters. Under the ECI's new order, ASDD voters can submit enumeration forms to the electoral registration officer or assistant officer where they now live, downloading the form with their EPIC number from the CEO website or ECINET.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: The figures come from the Maharashtra CEO via a Hindi wire report and have not been cross-checked in English sources.

items.text: Speaking in Dehradun on Uttarakhand's foundation day, Home Minister Amit Shah called Rahul Gandhi's 'Vote Bachao' yatra a 'save the infiltrators' yatra. He asked why Congress opposes cleaning infiltrators off the voter rolls, and said the Centre is ready for a special Parliament session to debate SIR. Rahul Gandhi replied on X that Shah should get PM Modi to debate him openly, and that he would do so on any platform at any time. BJP MP Tejasvi Surya led a BJP protest in Mangaluru, accusing Congress of undermining constitutional bodies.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Organiser (RSS-affiliated) uses Shah's infiltrator framing in its headline and includes no Congress reply. ANI wire copy carries both sides. Congress-leaning coverage (National Herald, Jairam Ramesh) presents SIR as mass disenfranchisement. Swarajya had no new piece in the window.

items.text: Rahul Gandhi hosted senior AICC office-bearers, CWC members, state in-charges, and state Congress chiefs and legislature-party leaders at his residence on Nov 6. The party billed it as a 'Diwali Milan'. Reports beforehand said SIR protests, the 2027 state elections and the winter session were on the informal agenda. No decisions were announced. Pawan Khera said SIR could cost people documents and welfare access, Ashok Gehlot mocked the BJP's street protests as a ruling party, and Udit Raj blamed the BJP for Delhi's smog.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Congress says a rally against 'vote chori' is planned at Ramlila Maidan on Dec 14 (Deccan Herald headline, not read in full).

items.text: On Nov 6 the Commission for Air Quality Management invoked Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan across Delhi-NCR as a precaution before Diwali, about four days after Stage II. Stage III bans non-essential construction and demolition, including road works, and restricts older polluting vehicles, with hybrid classes advised for junior grades. Delhi's AQI was 364–365 ('very poor') on Saturday morning, after 382 in Friday's 4 pm CPCB bulletin. IIT Delhi (440), Bawana and Dwarka (410) and Noida (425) were 'severe'. The IITM early-warning system forecasts 'severe' air on Nov 7–9. The Supreme Court allows certified green crackers only on Nov 7–8, 6–7 am and 8–10 pm, with the full ban back from Nov 9.
items.notes: The full list of Stage III curbs comes from The Week. The CAQM order text was not read. The cracker hours come from ThePrint/PTI headlines on the earlier SC order.

items.text: Punjab recorded 357 new stubble-burning cases on Nov 6, bringing the season total since Sept 15 to 3,144. Tarn Taran (611), Firozpur (410) and Sangrur (281) lead.
items.notes: The figures are probably from the Punjab Remote Sensing Centre, but that is not confirmed.

items.text: Karnataka Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad said tests on 14 petrol samples from seven districts found ethanol above the 20% E20 limit in 11 of them, up to 31.2% at an IOCL outlet. Bengaluru's Shriram Research Institute ran the tests after oil-company labs left ethanol content out of their reports. The state wants an explanation from the Centre, action against oil companies, ethanol content shown at the pump and a choice of blends, and puts the cost to motorists at about Rs 1 lakh crore a year. In a joint statement, IOCL, BPCL and HPCL rejected the claims. They said the October sampling was done without their representatives and outside statutory procedures, that they never received counter-samples or lab details, and that their E20 meets IS 17021.
items.notes: Both sides were read. The Rs 1.01 lakh crore figure is the state's estimate built on assumptions. No Petroleum Ministry statement was found. This sets a Congress state government against central PSUs.

items.text: Rahul Gandhi seized on Karnataka's fuel tests on Nov 7. He accused the Modi government of misleading consumers and said 'E20 has become 420' (slang for fraud), arguing that motorists pay for petrol but get more ethanol, which hurts mileage and engines. The government had not responded by the time of reporting.
items.notes: The UNI copy is partly paywalled. The oil companies' rebuttal is in the previous event.

items.text: Farmer groups called a statewide bandh in Karnataka over sugarcane prices, demanding Rs 5,500 a tonne, with protests in several districts. Mill owners went to court for protection of crushing operations. CM D.K. Shivakumar said fixing cane and sugar prices is the Centre's job. He said he had written to and spoken with PM Modi, that Union Minister Pralhad Joshi had promised to work toward a solution, and that he would raise the issue when Modi visits Bengaluru on Nov 13.
items.notes: IANS-based headlines (thehawk.in, hiindia.com) say the farmers withdrew the protest. Those articles could not be fetched, so the withdrawal and any agreed price are unconfirmed.

items.text: Air Vice Marshal Shekhar Yadav of the IAF's Eastern Air Command set out terms for the Agniveer 'second tour of duty'. Fixed pay would be Rs 43,500 a month in the fifth year and Rs 47,500 in the sixth, plus allowances. Seva Nidhi contributions over the two years would total Rs 10.92 lakh before interest (Rs 3.28 lakh from the Agniveer, Rs 7.64 lakh from the government). He said all willing Agniveers who finish the second tour can then compete for regular enrolment on objective criteria. No gazette notification or formal order has been published.
items.notes: Dated Nov 5, before this window, but not in previous logs. It partly answers watch W-261106-12 (pay and Seva Nidhi), but the source is a service officer's statement, not a PIB release or gazette.

items.text: The Supreme Court refused to stay a Gujarat High Court order upholding a ban on non-vegetarian food within 500 m of the Somnath temple. It asked the High Court to decide the pending appeals, preferably within two months.
items.notes: Taken from the LiveLaw listing. The full article could not be fetched.

items.text: The Supreme Court admitted DMK leader K.R. Periakaruppan's appeal against a Madras High Court ruling that upheld TVK's Seenivasa Sethupathi's one-vote win in Tirupattur. The court ordered the election records preserved.
items.notes: Taken from the LiveLaw listing.

items.text: Amar Ujala reports that the Calcutta High Court has stopped notification of Kolkata Municipal Corporation elections until it rules on a challenge to ward delimitation. LiveLaw earlier reported that the court had barred the state from notifying the polls until Nov 6 and reserved orders.
items.notes: The extension of the restraint past Nov 6 rests on an Amar Ujala live-blog headline.

items.text: Foreign investors bought a net Rs 15,000 crore (about $1.6bn) of Indian shares on Nov 5, their biggest single-day net purchase in nearly six years, helping fuel the Diwali-week rally. RBI data released on Nov 6 showed forex reserves down $2.69bn to $717.06bn in the week to Oct 30, which reports link to the RBI selling dollars to support the rupee. A special one-hour Muhurat trading session for Samvat 2083 is set for Sunday, Nov 8 (2:20–3:30 pm).
items.outlet: HDFC Sky; National Herald (PTI); Choice India
items.notes: The Nov 6 Sensex/Nifty close is already logged. The FII figure is provisional exchange data as relayed by a broker site. The Muhurat time is from broker notes, not the exchange circular.

items.text: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh is spending Diwali eve with troops in Darjeeling district (Bagdogra and Sukna) and plans to visit the Sherathang war memorial in Sikkim on Nov 8.

The 10th Ayodhya Deepotsav opens on Nov 7 with Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan, CM Yogi Adityanath and Governor Anandiben Patel attending. Plans include lighting diyas on 56 ghats of the Sarayu, a laser and drone show, and about 2,000 artists from 13 states. Reported diya counts vary between 30 lakh and 3 million.

PAP and Interia report that the Pentagon has confirmed Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz will meet Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday Nov 10, at 10:30 Washington time (16:30 in Poland). The agenda covers US bases and troop presence in Poland and the alliance more broadly. Deputy Minister Sobkowiak-Czarnecka said the permanent-base talks are on track but several steps remain, and the final decision rests with Trump.
items.notes: The September meeting was cancelled at short notice. Hegseth faces a possible impeachment push from Rep. Massie, who is expected to decide early next week.

items.text: In an IANS interview, Poland's ambassador to India, Piotr Świtalski, said relations entered 'a new phase' after Tusk's October visit to New Delhi. By his account, the visit produced 13 contracts, MoUs or letters of intent, and business forums in New Delhi and Bengaluru drew more than 100 Polish and nearly 200 Indian firms. He said India's support for Poland's bid to become a permanent G20 member is very valuable.
items.notes: Published Nov 5, before this window, and not logged earlier. The figures are the ambassador's own and the deals are not itemised.

items.text: President Trump took part in a Diwali celebration in the Oval Office on Nov 6, with India's Ambassador Vinay Kwatra present, PTI reported. The PTI report carried no remarks from Trump on Modi, the trade deal or a Manila meeting.
items.notes: Other outlets (Deccan Herald, india.com) mention Indian-American CEOs attending. Those were not read.

items.text: Telangana student Sreeja Reddy Koya has been missing in Boston since Nov 2. A Telangana minister has asked authorities to help find her.
items.notes: The minister's name was given only as 'K.V. Reddy'. Not verified.
